posting.description:
What you’ll be part of
Garner is on a mission to transform the U.S. healthcare system — and we’re the only proven player doing exactly that. We partner with employers to redesign how healthcare works: applying 550+ proprietary clinical metrics across 80+ specialties to a dataset of 320M+ patients to identify the best-performing doctors, then using compelling incentives to steer members to the care that helps them get healthier, faster.
The result is a rare “win win” — better care and lower costs for both members and employers. In just five years, our work has helped over 2.5 million people access higher-quality care and saved $1B in healthcare costs. We recently raised our Series E and have doubled five years running. If you've ever wanted your work to solve a problem that touches every person in this country, this is the opportunity to do exactly that. You'd be joining a team fundamentally reimagining healthcare in the U.S. — and using AI to scale that impact further and faster than anyone else can.
Who we want
We are seeking exceptional Software Engineering Interns for our 10-week summer program in New York City. As a core member of our engineering team, you'll build and launch features that directly impact real people — helping our members find top doctors and manage medical claims with ease.
You'll work alongside a passionate, multidisciplinary team of engineers, designers, and product managers, taking ownership of meaningful problems in a fast-paced, agile environment. This is hands-on experience building the systems that power our mission: transforming the healthcare economy to deliver high-quality, affordable care for all.
Select interns will be offered full-time roles upon successful completion of the program.
What you will do
Use AI to build, optimize, and maintain software systems
Collaborate across disciplines to understand our domain and iterate on projects
Participate in code reviews, sharing your insights and learning from others
Engage in problem solving sessions with senior engineers and team leads where your unique perspective will be valued
Deliver a capstone project presentation to engineering leaders and business stakeholders, demonstrating your work and impact
What we're looking for
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science or related STEM field (expected graduation Fall 2027–Spring 2028)
Solid CS fundamentals with exposure to front-end (JavaScript, React) or back-end (Python, Node.js) technologies; familiarity with databases or cloud platforms (AWS, Docker) is a plus
Exposure to or interest in building with AI coding agents (we use Claude Code) is a plus
Strong problem-solver who enjoys breaking down challenges and finding elegant solutions
Self-starter who takes ownership of their work and is motivated by real-world impact
Clear communicator who can discuss technical ideas with both technical and non-technical audiences, and takes feedback well
Excited by fast-paced environments and eager to stretch their skills
A desire to do work that matters: and to be held to a high standard while doing it. You're energized by a mission with measurable outcomes, not just good intentions. You engage with AI tools as part of how you do your best work, and hold yourself accountable to outcomes that matter beyond your team’s metrics
What you’ll get here
You’ll work on problems that matter, at a company working to change healthcare at scale. You’ll work at the intersection of AI and systemic healthcare reform, where the problems we solve are as interesting and compelling as the mission.
At Garner, you’ll take on real, ambitious problems with real ownership and autonomy, alongside exceptional, principles-based people who genuinely want you to win. It’s demanding by design. You’ll be challenged to stretch beyond what you thought possible and receive consistent coaching to help you grow and do the best work of your career. This isn't the right fit for everyone, and that's intentional. The people here are driven by what's at stake for real people, and that's what gives our intensity its purpose.
Technologies we use
Claude Code, Kubernetes, AWS, Airflow, dlt, dbt, Python, TypeScript, React, Go
Please note: we are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.
Compensation
The weekly pay rate for this role is $2,400. In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for a housing stipend.
Few roles offer this combination: work that is genuinely hard, a mission that is genuinely important, and a team that is genuinely invested in your success. If that’s what you’re looking for, we’d love to meet you.

posting.description:
About the company
General Matter enriches uranium.
We are designing, building, and operating the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services, here in the US.
In the process, we are restoring America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel to power AI, advanced manufacturing and critical industries our country relies on to remain competitive.
Fuel drives the cost of advanced reactor electricity production, and enrichment drives the cost of the fuel that advanced reactors consume. Reliable, low-cost enrichment is the catalyst for the nuclear Renaissance now under way.
Our mission is to make nuclear not only the cleanest and safest source of baseload power, but also the most affordable. We believe abundant nuclear energy will lead to a post-scarcity society.
We were incubated inside Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by over a dozen of the world's top venture capital firms.
Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production.
We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency.
Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.
About This Role
As a General Matter Software Engineering Intern, you will help develop performant, safe, and high-quality software. Your work will support code where reliability, performance, and safety are of utmost importance. You will work closely with cross-functional teams, including electrical engineers, software engineers, chemical engineers, manufacturing engineers, nuclear engineers, materials scientists, and physicists. If you seek high-impact work and are excited by fast-paced, intense, Skunkworks-style projects, we encourage you to reach out to join our team.
We're hiring interns across three focus areas:
Backend interns will help build high-performance services and APIs that coordinate control systems, manage state across distributed hardware, and expose interfaces for monitoring and operations.
Distributed systems interns will support the development of fault-tolerant coordination systems, real-time data pipelines processing high-throughput sensor telemetry, and the infrastructure that keeps critical systems running reliably at scale.
Tooling interns will help build the developer platforms, CI/CD systems, observability tools, and deployment infrastructure that let our team iterate rapidly and safely in a production environment where mistakes have physical consequences.
Responsibilities
Assist in designing and implementing high-performance software systems in C++ and Python, with a focus on reliability and maintainability.
Support the architecture of solutions, contributing to decisions around system design, performance trade-offs, and technology selection.
Participate in technical design reviews and code reviews, learning and helping uphold engineering best practices across the team.
Help build and maintain automated testing and CI/CD pipelines to support software quality at scale.
Work closely with senior engineers, contributing to progress on complex, ambiguous technical problems.
Basic Qualifications
Current undergraduate or graduate student pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline.
Proficiency in C++ and/or Python.
Strong CS fundamentals, such as algorithms, data structures, concurrency, and system design.
Collaborative team member who thrives in fast-paced, multidisciplinary environments and is eager to learn.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Exposure to distributed systems, observability tooling, or infrastructure as code.
Experience with Python ecosystems for data pipelines, automation, or backend services.
Coursework or project experience with C++ performance optimization, profiling, or low-level systems programming.
Familiarity with Linux system programming, including threading models, IPC, or low-level kernel interfaces.
Evidence of exceptional ability (prior projects, portfolio of work, completed products, etc).
Additional Requirements
Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.
Equal Opportunity Employer
General Matter is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with General Matter is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.
Compensation and Benefits
The hourly pay range for this internship is
$32–$46
per hour, depending on the candidate's current standing in school (i.e. sophomore, senior).
Interns will receive a monthly housing stipend and are eligible for overtime pay. Please note that the stated hourly range is an estimate and may be adjusted based on market conditions, business needs, or other factors.

HP IQ's AI Machine Learning (AML) team is building the foundational platform powering a new generation of agentic devices. posting.description:
At Hudl, we build great teams. We hire the best of the best to ensure you’re working with people you can constantly learn from. You’re trusted to get your work done your way while testing the limits of what’s possible and what’s next. We work hard to provide a culture where everyone feels supported, and our employees feel it—their votes helped us become one of
Newsweek's Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces
.
We think of ourselves as the team behind the team, supporting the lifelong impact sports can have: the lessons in teamwork and dedication; the influence of inspiring coaches; and the opportunities to reach new heights. That’s why we help teams from all over the world see their game differently. Our products make it easier for coaches and athletes at any level to capture video, analyze data, share highlights and more.
Ready to join us?
Your Role
We’re looking for Software Engineering interns to join us at Hudl’s headquarters in Lincoln, Nebraska. You’ll ship real code to our users, work alongside experienced engineers and cross-functional software teams, and learn what modern software development actually looks like.
As a Software Engineer Intern, you’ll:
Contribute to real projects, deliver meaningful impact
. You’ll contribute to features and tools used by coaches, athletes, and fans around the world, from platform improvements to new capabilities for our users.
Modern engineering practices
. You’ll work across our tech stack using concepts like microservices architecture, CI/CD, and agentic AI workflows.
Receive mentorship and growth
. You’ll learn from and work with experienced engineers and team members who are invested in your development through code reviews, design discussions, and hands-on guidance.
Location
Our priority is to hire product interns who have the ability to
live in Lincoln, Nebraska for the 2027 summer
. We’ll cover your housing costs. Need to travel to Lincoln? We'll cover that too.
Must-Haves
A current student.
We’re welcoming degree-seeking students in computer science, software engineering or computer engineering to join our team.
Enthusiastic
. You’re eager to gain experience by shipping code to production (yeah, production) in a fast-paced environment.
Collaborative.
You understand that the best software is built by teams, not individuals. You're ready to participate in design discussions, give and receive feedback on code reviews, and learn from your peers.
A continuous learner.
Technology is always evolving, and so are you. You're curious and motivated to pick up new languages, frameworks, and skills, and you're excited about how AI is reshaping what it means to build software.
Nice-to-Haves
Full-stack web applications
. You’ll likely be working in C# / .NET and Javascript / React in this role. It can help if you have experience using these technologies.
Passionate
. You take pride in your course projects, side projects and/or open source contributions.
Innovative
. You hate the idea of being a cog in the machine. You want to own your features.
Our Role
Ask you to make an impact.
You're part of the team—that means you'll have real responsibilities. We want to hear what you think and see what you can do.
Provide an environment to help you succeed.
We've invested in our offices, designing incredible spaces with our employees in mind. But even if you’re taking advantage of the opportunity to work remotely, we’ll provide you the tech you need to do your best work.
Develop your career.
On top of working alongside some of the best professionals in the business and gaining real-world experience, we’ll give you extra opportunities like lunch-and-learns and access to curated libraries to round out your internship.
Support your wellbeing.
You’ll have an entire team on your side to give advice and provide answers to your questions, plus more resources like topic-specific Slack channels and employee resource groups. In short, we have you covered.

We believe in a transparent and efficient hiring process, and we value the time and effort you invest in this process. We’re committed to keeping you informed along the way.

Integra is hiring entrepreneurial and quantitatively-skilled students/graduates with data analytics experience who are interested in translating their academic interests into the real-world applications to identify, investigate and analyze fraud in various domains, including finance, healthcare and cryptocurrencies. Integra is a boutique economic consulting and forensic analytics firm that has worked with government agencies and private entities to analyze many complex and high-profile schemes. Our team applies data science and econometric techniques and intensely values each employee to take initiative and to be curious while operating as a data detective to solve complex problems. Our main office is also conveniently located adjacent to the UT Austin campus which enables us to closely interface with the academic environment and the university’s top intellectual talent.
As an intern you will code software used to automate processes, scrape and collect large data sets, and perform advanced econometric analysis. You will have flexibility in the programming language used, but scripting languages such as R, Python, and SQL are used most often. The internship is also designed to give you:
Exposure to how technical degrees such as economics, statistics, finance, engineering, computer science, and physics are used in industry
Opportunities to work on team-based and individual projects
Visibility to industry experts
Job Qualifications:

Proficiency in Microsoft Excel
Attention to detail with big-picture understanding
Ability to work well in teams
Highest ethical standards
All education levels (Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D.) welcome

posting.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.
The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.
With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.
The Role
We’re looking for a stellar Electrical Engineering Intern to join our team for a 3 month internship. Working closely with our engineers, you will be responsible for developing novel electrical designs spanning from PCBAs to full systems. You will work hands-on with novel power, digital, and mixed signal designs used across the satellite while getting exposure to other subsystems within the engineering organization. K2 Space is a highly collaborative environment and our interns will be encouraged to work with mentors and other team members to execute complex projects.
Responsibilities
Design electronics PCBAs for spacecraft including architecture, component selection, circuit board design, board bring up and debugging
Qualify your designs through environmental testing including vibration, shock, thermal, and thermal vacuum testing
Work with internal and external stakeholders to integrate your designs into the spacecraft systems and operate your hardware in flight
Develop test equipment, development PCBAs, and test scripts to assist with all of the above
Qualifications
Must be currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in electrical or computer engineering
6+ months experience of technical engineering skills outside of the university setting classroom (eg: laboratory, research, extracurricular project teams, volunteering, personal projects or prior internship/work experience)
Nice to Have
Ability to work well in an integrated collaborative team environment, including frequent interactions with technicians, engineers, and managers
Experience designing multi-layer PCBAs for high-speed digital applications
Experience with high performance kW scale isolated power converter design
Experience designing analog control loops, solid state load switches, motor inverters, EMI/EMC compliance, or sensor signal conditioning circuits
Experience with digital processors, FPGAs, memory chips, or network switches
Proficient with circuit simulation tools such as LTspiceE
Experience with load switch design and power path protection schemes
Experience programming in C/C++, Python, or Matlab
Compensation
Hourly pay range for this non-exempt role is $30 - $40 per hour
Hourly rate will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level
Housing and travel stipend may also be available
If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, we encourage you to still apply! Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other and non-traditional career twists and turns are encouraged!
If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.
Export Compliance
As defined in the ITAR, “U.S. Persons” include U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (i.e., Green Card holders), and certain protected individuals (e.g., refugees/asylees, American Samoans). Please consult with a knowledgeable advisor if you are unsure whether you are a “U.S. Person.”
The person hired for this role will have access to information and items controlled by U.S. export control regulations, including the export control regulations outlined in the International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR). The person hired for this role must therefore either be a “U.S. person” as defined by
22 C.F.R. § 120.15
or otherwise eligible for a federally issued export control license.
Equal Opportunity

and

Available for a minimum 12 week internship in person at our HQ in Torrance

posting.description:
Katalyst Description:
Katalyst is an American technology company
focused on d
ynamic space operations
.
We are building a fleet of
dual-use multipurpose
robotic space vehicles
to
creat
e the
future where maneuvering, upgrading, refueling,
resupply
and exploration are as routine as they are on Earth. Getting to space and overcoming the gravity well is only half the story. What you do there is the future. We are not building the trains. We are building the machines that lay down the tracks. By developing the foundational capabilities that make sustained, responsive operations possible, we enable a new era of space
exploration
that strengthens national security and ensures freedom of action in an increasingly contested domain.
Katalyst Culture:
Working at Katalyst is intense, hands-on, and deeply rewarding. You’ll take real ownership and see your work move from concept to operations in an environment where the problems are hard and the impact is real. We value humility, craftsmanship, and doing things the right way, even when it’s harder. You’ll work closely with thoughtful, driven teammates who push each other to do their best.
What You’ll Do
Contribute to real spacecraft engineering work in one of four technical tracks: Electrical, Mechanical, GNC, or Software, with assignments sized appropriately for an internship.
Work alongside experienced engineers on scoped technical problems involving design, analysis, implementation, integration, test, simulation, debugging, or engineering documentation.
Gain hands-on exposure to flight hardware, test equipment, software environments, simulations, engineering data, and the processes used to take spacecraft from concept through test and operations.
Participate in design reviews, test activities, technical discussions, and team meetings; ask thoughtful questions and communicate progress, assumptions, risks, and blockers clearly.
Collaborate across disciplines to understand how electrical, mechanical, software, controls, mission operations, and program constraints interact at the spacecraft level.
Apply classroom fundamentals to real engineering decisions and compare models, calculations, code, or design intent against test results and practical constraints.
Document analyses, code, drawings, procedures, test results, or technical decisions so the work can be reviewed and used by the broader team.
Demonstrate increasing independence over the course of the internship while seeking feedback early and maintaining ownership of assigned work.
Create repeatable capture and partnership mechanisms that allow Katalyst to scale national security business development without becoming dependent on informal relationships or individual heroics.
What We’re Looking For
Required
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Robotics, Applied Math, Physics, or a closely related technical field.
Strong academic foundation in the fundamentals relevant to the selected discipline and the ability to explain technical reasoning clearly.
Demonstrated technical interest through coursework, laboratories, research, student teams, capstone work, personal projects, prior internships, or other hands-on experience.
Ability to break down a technical problem, identify assumptions, ask useful questions, and make progress with guidance from more experienced engineers.
Clear written and verbal communication and the ability to distinguish personal contributions from the work of a broader team.
Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar tools, systems, and technical domains quickly.
Ability to collaborate effectively, receive direct technical feedback, and follow through reliably on commitments.
Ability to comply with applicable export-control requirements and customer-access restrictions.
Your Ideal Background
Preferred
Prior internship, co-op, research, student-team, or project experience in spacecraft, aerospace, robotics, autonomous systems, defense technology, high-reliability hardware, or another technically demanding environment.
Experience designing, building, coding, analyzing, testing, or debugging something beyond normal classroom problem sets.
Electrical track: exposure to circuits, embedded systems, PCB design, power electronics, sensors, test equipment, controls hardware, or hardware-in-the-loop environments.
Mechanical track: exposure to CAD, mechanisms, structures, thermal or structural analysis, manufacturing, GD&T, test fixtures, or hardware integration.
GNC track: exposure to dynamics, controls, estimation, navigation, orbital mechanics, simulation, MATLAB/Simulink, Python, or C/C++.
Software track: exposure to C/C++, Python, Linux, embedded or real-time software, networking, testing, simulation, robotics, autonomy, or mission / ground software.
Additional Requirements: Must be available for the defined internship term and willing to work hands-on in the office, lab, integration, or test environment as required. Occasional extended hours may be needed during critical test or mission activities.
Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at Katalyst. You will also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of the Employee Stock Option and Equity Plan, as well as a relocation bonus and other discretionary bonuses. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, and unlimited Paid Time Off.
At Katalyst our work on projects involving the U.S. Department of Defense requires adherence to International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 C.F.R. Parts 120-130, which requires compliance with U.S. export laws before allowing employees to perform certain positions. Currently, our available roles necessitate access to ITAR-controlled information, and as a result, Katalyst would have to ensure any non-US person is authorized access to ITAR information before the commencement of employment. We are committed to equal employment opportunities and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.

posting.description:
At Klaviyo, we value the unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives each Klaviyo (we call ourselves Klaviyos) brings to our workplace each and every day. We believe everyone deserves a fair shot at success and appreciate the experiences each person brings beyond the traditional job requirements. If you’re a close but not exact match with the description, we hope you’ll still consider applying.
At Klaviyo, our Engineering teams build scalable, high-performance systems that power both our product and the infrastructure behind it. As a Software Engineering Intern, you'll be part of a fast-paced, collaborative team whose work reaches thousands of customers worldwide. You won't just be writing code. You'll be solving hard problems, shaping how users experience our product, and learning from engineers who've been doing this for a while.
This internship is your shot to put your software development skills to work in production. You'll be embedded on one of our engineering teams (see overviews below), take on projects that matter to our customers, and build a technical foundation as you make connections across the business.
Our interns come from all kinds of coding backgrounds, but they all share one thing: they're excited to build, own, and scale features end-to-end, from scratch. You'll work alongside experienced engineers, take on hard technical problems, and ship code that supports Klaviyo's mission. We're an AI-first company, so you'll be expected to use AI tools to support your work, learn faster, and do your best work here.
How you'll make an impact
Own features that our 180K+ paying customers rely on daily to reach their consumers and grow their business.
Take responsibility for the mission, technical direction, and operation of projects with immediate impact.
Own the full lifecycle of your code: writing it, testing it, shipping it, and making it better over time. Ownership is expected here, not just encouraged.
Build and ship features that meet a high bar and grow your technical skills while you do it.
Get hands-on debugging real issues, both locally and in production.
Contribute to documentation and support your team during incidents (real-world problems teach you things a tutorial never will).
Work closely with your teammates: ask questions, share ideas, and get better by taking feedback seriously.
Learn to use the right tool for the job, lean into AI, and keep looking for ways to make things better.
Put AI at the center of how you work to move faster. Build smarter systems and better workflows from the ground up.
Who you are
At least one previous software engineering internship or co-op, with hands-on software development experience
Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Math/Statistics, or a related field
Graduating in December 2027 or May/June 2028
Experience with some of these technologies and languages:
Python, Django, Typescript, React, Go
MySQL, Cassandra, Clickhouse, Kafka, Redis
Amazon Web Services (EC2, RDS, Aurora, etc.), Terraform
You enjoy working across new technologies and you’re excited to work across the stack from back-end to front-end work
You love digging into performance and scalability issues to find breakthrough solutions: a slow-loading UI, too many clicks in a workflow, a database query timing out, a queue that won't drain. You believe every problem can be solved, and you'd rather run toward it than around it.
You enjoy shipping code early and often, working closely with products to build better software based on feedback from thousands of end users.
You embrace Klaviyo's "always learning" culture. We learn faster together, which is part of why this program happens in person.
You've already experimented with AI in work or personal projects, and you're excited to find ways to make your work smarter and more efficient.
Internship logistics
Our Summer Internship Program is an 11-week paid experience [June 1–August 13] at our Boston, MA headquarters. Interns are in office 5 days a week.
Offers will be team agnostic - interns are placed on a team approximately 30 days from the start of the program. Team placement can be on a full-stack, back-end, or front-end team within any of the pillars.
Before joining individual teams, all interns go through Klaviyo Base Camp, our onboarding experience built to get you up to speed on Klaviyo, our product, and the day-to-day of engineering here, plus time to get to know the other interns. You'll join your team ready to dive into real project work from day one.
Our Boston office is genuinely fun. Lunch is on us 5 days a week, along with free snacks and drinks, ping pong, Nintendo Switch, a golf simulator, and a speakeasy to unwind in.
Throughout the summer, interns get together for social events beyond team and project work: a Red Sox game, a Boston Harbor Cruise, trips to Kings and Versus, ice cream socials, and Ask Me Anything sessions with Klaviyo's senior leadership.
Apply before October 7 if you can. We interview and hire on a rolling basis.
Former intern projects
Built a new 'Share Inbox Preview' feature allowing users to generate public share links from the Email Editor.
Implemented an 'Invite Expiration Extension' endpoint in IAM with basic logging and validation.
Created a small dashboard that displays real-time delivery stats using existing API data and simple visualizations.
Migrated one internal service from Jenkins → Buildkite and documented the migration process.
Added an image and carousel support for WhatsApp Templates ensuring backward compatibility.
Engineering at Klaviyo
Our engineering teams are organized into pillars to keep the work focused.
Data Infrastructure:
Empower our internal teams and customers to get the best out of our data and agent platforms. underlying capabilities: Agent Platform, CDP revenue, Data Lake usage, Active API endpoints, Accounts with healthy API usage
MCMI:
Own the growth, revenue, and reliability of our mobile channels and all messaging infrastructure.
Core Infrastructure:
Empower our internal engineering, sales, and service teams to be as effective as possible by improving productivity of the eng, product, and design teams.
Growth Marketing Platform
: Give marketers the tools they need to engage with their customers, be successful, and know where they stand.
AI & Analytics:
Applies AI, data, and analytics to automate work, surface insights, and help customers make smarter decisions that maximize Klaviyo Attributed Value (KAV).
Autonomous Service:
Builds AI-powered customer service experiences that help resolve issues, support transactions, and connect customers with human assistance when needed.
If you're excited about this role but your background doesn't check every box, apply anyway. Some of the strongest Klaviyos didn't start with a perfect resume match.

posting.description:
Lexington Medical, Inc. is hiring an Electrical/Embedded Software Engineering Intern for Summer 2027 at our headquarters in Bedford, MA. You will join our R&D team and gain hands-on experience developing the embedded hardware and software behind our AEON™ surgical stapling platform. Depending on your background and project needs, your work may span electrical design, embedded firmware, PCB development, hardware bring-up, testing, debugging, and hardware-software integration.
About Lexington Medical
Lexington Medical, Inc. is a medical device company designing and manufacturing surgical stapling technology at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, just outside Boston. Our AEON™ Endostapler is an FDA-cleared, minimally invasive surgical stapler used in operating rooms around the world.
With electrical, software, mechanical, manufacturing, and quality teams working closely together under one roof, interns stay close to the product and see how engineering concepts move through development, prototyping, testing, verification, manufacturing, and ultimately into the operating room.
About the Internship
As an Electrical/ Embedded Software Engineering Intern at Lexington Medical, you will work alongside our R&D engineers developing embedded systems for electromechanical surgical devices. You will contribute to real engineering projects involving the interaction between electronics, embedded firmware, motors, sensors, and physical mechanisms.
Depending on your experience and interests, you may work more heavily on electrical hardware, embedded software, or projects that cross both areas. This could include designing and testing circuits, supporting PCB development, writing and debugging embedded code, bringing up new hardware, integrating sensors and motors, or troubleshooting complete electromechanical systems.
This is a good fit for a student who likes understanding how hardware and software work together and wants to build, test, debug, and improve real products rather than work only in simulation or theory.
Responsibilities:
Support the development and testing of embedded electrical and software systems.
Develop, test, and debug embedded firmware using C/C++.
Assist with schematic capture, PCB design, and component selection.
Support hardware bring-up, bench testing, and system-level debugging.
Work with microcontrollers, sensors, motors, actuators, and other electromechanical components.
Use electrical test equipment to troubleshoot hardware and firmware.
Collaborate with electrical, software, mechanical, and manufacturing engineers.
Support engineering testing, verification, and technical documentation.
Qualifications:
Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related technical field.
Coursework or project experience with embedded systems, electronics, microcontrollers, PCB design, firmware, or robotics.
Experience programming in C or C++.
Hands-on experience building, testing, or debugging hardware or embedded systems.
Prior internship, co-op, research, or substantial hands-on project experience preferred.
Strong problem-solving, communication, and attention to detail.
What Success Looks Like
By the middle of the summer, you can contribute to day-to-day electrical and embedded software engineering work with increasing independence and understand how hardware, firmware, and electromechanical systems work together.
By the end of the internship, you have completed a meaningful electrical, embedded software, or hardware-software integration project that the engineering team can continue using after you leave.
You leave with concrete examples of hardware or firmware you developed, technical problems you solved, and engineering decisions you made on a real medical device.
Program Details
Timing:
June 2027 through August 2027, approximately three months.
Schedule:
Full-time, five days per week on-site in Bedford, Massachusetts.
Location & Work Arrangement
This internship is based at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, in the Greater Boston area, and is fully on-site five days per week.
Visit
our
Candidate Journey page
to learn what to expect from our hiring process.
Hourly Rate
$32
—
$36 USD

posting.description:
Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads.
Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter!
If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders.
Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light!
The Packaging team at Lightmatter
We are building the world's first photonic engine for AI at scale, and packaging is where the physics meets the product. Our Silicon Packaging team works at the intersection of electrical, mechanical, optical, and thermal engineering to bring co-packaged optics from concept to high-volume production.
We're hiring across all levels from juniors undergrads to PhD candidates for both internship and full-time new grad positions. Wherever you are in your academic journey, you'll work on real problems from day one alongside engineers who have shipped leading-edge products at the world's most demanding semiconductor in the world. Why should you apply? To have the best and most interesting internship experience! Packaging at Lightmatter means working on co-packaged optics for the AI infrastructure that doesn't exist yet and helping build the team and methods that will make it real.
Responsibilities
Depending on your background, you'll contribute to one or more of these areas:
Signal & Power Integrity — high-speed interface analysis (PCIe, UCIe, SerDes), PDN design and simulation, eye diagrams, jitter, S-parameters
Thermal Engineering — CFD simulation, heat sink and TIM evaluation, liquid cooling, package-level thermal analysis
Mechanical & Thermo-Mechanical Design — structural analysis, tolerance stack-up, GD&T, FEA, solder fatigue, CTE mismatch
Packaging Integration — 2.5D/3D packaging, fiber attach, heterogeneous integration, assembly yield and reliability
Qualifications
Pursuing or recently completed a BS, MS, or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field
Hands-on experience through coursework, capstone projects, research labs, or internships
Familiarity with at least one relevant tool — SolidWorks, ANSYS, ADS, Cadence, Python, MATLAB, or similar
Curious, collaborative, and comfortable asking questions
We offer competitive compensation. The base salary range for this role determined based on location, experience, educational background, and market data.
Hourly Range
$40
—
$67 USD

Comprehensive Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
Retirement Savings Matching Program
Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary & AD&D)
Generous Time Off (Vacation, Sick & Public Holidays)
Paid Family Leave
Short Term & Long Term Disability
Training & Development
Commuter Benefits
Flexible, hybrid workplace model
Equity grants (applicable to full-time employees)

posting.description:
Technical Program Manager Intern, Hardware Engineering
Program Managers (PMs) at Lunar Energy lead complex engineering programs from initial concept through to volume manufacturing. As a Technical Program Manager (TPM) Intern on the Hardware Engineering team, you'll get hands-on experience supporting our products through bring-up testing, environmental and durability validation, failure analysis, and regulatory certification. You'll work closely with engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, and external partners, learning how a global team aligns around schedules, risk, and clear communication to ship reliable hardware. We're looking for someone who's excited about a more sustainable future and wants to see, firsthand, what it takes to bring that vision to market.
Lunar Energy was founded to transition homes to 100% clean energy—making our electricity greener, our air cleaner and our energy more safe, secure and reliable for all. We’re a fast-growing, global company building the world’s best clean energy products to electrify all homes and connect communities to form clean, resilient virtual power plants.
On a given day at Lunar, you'll likely:
Support program schedules by tracking milestones, flagging risks, and helping communicate progress across the engineering, reliability, test, and compliance teams.
Help build and maintain validation roadmaps, timelines, and deliverable trackers, and learn to define and track resource requirements alongside senior TPMs.
Sit in on test and certification reviews, capture action items, and follow up to make sure issues are driven to closure with clear ownership.
Help coordinate the ordering, shipment, and delivery of prototype validation builds, and track how build-to-build variation affects downstream test and compliance work.
Pull together clear, executive-ready status updates that summarize risk, progress, and next steps for a program.
Learn firsthand how program management drives a hardware product from concept through production, and how engineering, quality, and manufacturing teams work together to get there.
About you
You're currently pursuing a BS or MS in an engineering discipline (Mechanical, Electrical, Systems, Industrial, or related).
You're passionate about accelerating the adoption of renewables and improving our energy infrastructure, and you're excited to learn how ambitious program plans actually get executed.
Prior internship, co-op, or project experience in an engineering or technical environment (e.g., a lab, a formula/Solar/Baja or other collegiate design team, or a research group) is a plus.
You communicate clearly, ask good questions, and follow up until things are resolved.
You're comfortable with ambiguity and enjoy collaborating across teams and levels in a fast-moving startup environment.
Familiarity with tools such as Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, or Excel is a plus, but not required — we'll teach you.
This is a full-time, on-site internship based in Mountain View, CA,

Our goal is to ensure that all Lunar Energy employees are fairly compensated. Please note that the hourly range information that follows is a good faith estimate for this position provided pursuant to the Pay Transparency for Pay Equity Act for California applicants. The hourly range estimate for this position depending on level of experience is $30-$40 USD
The actual offer, reflecting the total compensation package will be at the company’s sole discretion, and determined by factors including but not limited to years of experience, job level, geographic location, and other relevant business considerations. Maven Securities is a leading proprietary trading firm that leverages sophisticated technology and quantitative analysis to trade in global financial markets. We specialise in options and derivatives market making, where your skills can be directly applied to have a real impact.
At Maven, we believe exceptional careers are built deliberately. Our intern programme is designed for a small number of high-potential individuals each year, combining comprehensive training, real responsibility, and long-term development. We don’t hire large classes with the expectation that only a few will succeed, we invest in every individual who joins the team.
Programme details:
Location:
London
Programme dates:
21st June - 20 August 2027
Application deadline:
21st October 2026
Key requirements:
You must have the right to work in the region you are applying for at the time of application
You must be a penultimate-year undergraduate or master’s student
You must not have applied for any other Maven programmes in this cycle
You’ll begin with a structured 2-week training programme, designed to prepare you for your project work. This initial phase focuses on building the technical foundations and domain knowledge needed for the projects.
Following training, you’ll transition on to a 7-week project, where you’ll continue to learn through hands-on experience. Intern projects allow you to learn new skills and experience what life is like in a Maven Technology team.

Be directly embedded in Maven engineering teams to work on real world problems
Have a direct impact on the day-to-day workings of a high performance trading firm
Collaborate directly with Developers and Traders

Progress through a structured onboarding programme with clear learning milestones
Build your foundation through theory and exercise-led training, led by Maven’s Head of Technology Training & Graduates
Gain in-depth insight to the work you could expect to be doing as a future Graduate Developer by attending desk shadowing opportunities with current Graduates, across a range of Technology teams
Our technical syllabus covers the fundamentals of some of Maven’s main programming languages, e.g. C++, C# and Python, as well as TypeScript and ReactWe will teach you how to use some of Maven’s in-house tools and systems. Maven utilises the latest technology in order to meet and exceed our demanding business challenges. We believe in using the right tool for the right job with a strong focus on engineering rigour
Attend regular check-ins with the Technology and Emerging Talent teams
Who you are:
Key criteria:
A genuine interest in software development and a curiosity to learn
Familiarity with one or more programming languages
A willingness to adopt and utilise emerging AI technologies
We’re looking for someone who is:
An entrepreneurial thinker
with the ability to generate ideas, take initiative and drive innovation
A critical problem solver and decision maker
who can analyse situations, think clearly and make effective decisions
An agile learner
who is able to quickly acquire knowledge, take on feedback, adapt and apply insights across different contexts
Able to synthesise information
, resolve conflicting inputs, see the bigger picture, and translate complex information into actionable recommendations
Collaborative and influential
, able to build trust, work effectively with others and positively impact the team
Results-focused and accountable
, taking ownership and delivering outcomes reliably
Why Maven?:
Dedicated In-House Trainers:
Gain the tools to succeed in a rapidly evolving market, where AI is integral to our strategy and daily operations. Our tailored curriculums are led by in-house experts and cover both technical and professional skills, as well as guidance on how to adopt AI best practices
Accelerate Your Career:
Over 9 weeks, you’ll progress your understanding of software development and have the opportunity to jump-start your Maven career by being considered for a full-time Graduate Developer role for the following year
Proven Pathways:
Benefit from our structured pipeline programmes that set you up for long-term success. Around a quarter of Maven’s workforce joined through an Emerging Talent Programme, with many staying from Spring Week through the Graduate Programme and beyond
Supported to Succeed
: We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can perform at your best. We offer recruitment support where needed, and employee resource groups that help build community across the firm
Grow with Guidance:
Enjoy regular feedback, structured review points, and informal off-desk chats. Everyone in our Emerging Talent Programmes is also paired with a Maven buddy for practical advice and day-to-day support
Make a Real Impact, Fast:
Interns are embedded directly into our tech teams, contributing to critical projects. In fact, recent interns contributed to the foundations of Maven's AI initiative, which includes creating agentic workflows for different business functions, improving Trader and Developer tooling
Maven is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse workforce and creating an inclusive environment. We welcome applications from all candidates regardless of background or identity.

Regular social events where you can get to know us, from welcome dinners and the Maven summer party to end-of-programme celebrations
Free daily breakfast and lunch in the office, as well as snacks and drinks

A forward-thinking environment in which AI is integral to our strategy and daily operations

posting.description:
Come join one of America’s fastest-growing insurance companies. Since 1848, National Life Group has aimed to keep our promises, providing families with stability in good times and in bad. Throughout that history, we have provided peace of mind to those families as they plan their futures.
Our mission extends beyond the insurance and annuities policies that we offer. We strive to make the world a better place through our grants from our charitable foundation, paid volunteer time for our employees, environmentally sustainable and healthy workplaces, and events that promote the work of nonprofits in our own backyard.
We foster a collaborative environment with opportunities for growth and encourage our associates to live our values:
Do good. Be good. Make good.
Please note that we do not offer visa sponsorship for this position.
POSITION SUMMARY:
At National Life Group, we are modernizing our business and evolving our customer experience through digital-first technology solutions. Our technology teams play a critical role in building, enhancing, and supporting the applications and platforms that enable our customers, agents, and employees to do business more effectively.
The IT Applications Development Intern will work within our Inforce Applications team and partner with developers, business analysts, product owners, and other technology professionals to develop, enhance, test, and support business applications. Depending on project needs, the intern may contribute to application development, system integrations, troubleshooting, production support, automation, and technical documentation.
This role provides hands-on exposure to enterprise application development and support within a large-scale technology environment. Minneapolis (Bloomington, MN)

Ongoing training is provided as part of the position to ensure expertise within the team and department. You will aspire to use new technologies and challenge yourself to develop innovative solutions.

Work closely with developers to communicate bugs found during test automation and bring them to resolution
Develop, troubleshoot, and debug software programs for web services, databases, applications, and tools
Write readable, maintainable, and efficient code
Collaborate with team members on best practices, code reviews, internal tools, and process improvements
Create and maintain documentation for related software, processes, and procedures

Passion to learn new technologies and develop applications

High energy, confident, ambitious, and self-motivated individual

Our Site Design team provides design services for retail, commercial, mixed-use, and residential land development projects, along with industrial, sports, schools, and other site development types. As a civil engineering student intern, you will perform meaningful, hands-on, real-world work that will transform your classroom experience and help you envision your future career. You’ll be part of our team, working for our clients on projects with our most experienced engineers. You’ll assist with creating construction plans for sites that can include site layout, grading, stormwater, and utilities in AutoCAD and Civil 3D. You may also perform research, write technical reports, and travel to job sites.

Pursuing a degree in civil engineering.

About Pacific Fusion
Pacific Fusion was founded in 2023 with the mission to power the world with abundant, affordable, clean energy.
We are rapidly designing and building a pulser-driven inertial fusion system to achieve net facility gain (more fusion energy output than stored energy input). In parallel, we are developing the key components required to build affordable fusion systems.
Our plans are ambitious. We have raised over $900M so far from incredible investors, resourcing us to deliver on these plans. We are bringing together the best scientists, engineers, and operators from the fusion community, hard tech industry, and other sectors. We are united by a shared sense of urgency to provide clean power for the world, particularly managing climate change while meeting growing global energy demand. You can read more about us in
this letter from our founders
.
Why This Role Matters
As a
Software Engineering Intern
, you will help build the user interfaces and backend software systems that allow engineers, scientists and operators to run the fusion demonstration facility. You will work closely with controls engineers, scientists, and operators to develop software that presents real-time system state, manages configuration and data, and supports safe facility operations.
What You'll Do
Develop and improve web-based user interfaces for:
System status and health monitoring
Experiment or facility configuration
Alerts, events, and diagnostics
Assist in building backend services that:
Serve real-time and historical facility data
Manage configuration, metadata, and system state
Interface with controls systems and data pipelines
Support integration between:
UI applications, backend APIs, and facility systems
Write clear, maintainable code and contribute to code reviews
Help test, debug, and validate software used in live environments

Coursework or experience in:
Software development fundamentals
Web or backend programming
Familiarity with at least one of:
TypeScript / JavaScript
Go or Python
Basic understanding of:
Client–server applications
APIs and data flow
SQL and NoSQL Databases

Able to work full time, onsite for a minimum of
12 consecutive weeks
beginning in

Experience with:

Git and collaborative development

Industrial systems, automation, or controls
Data visualization or real-time systems
Exposure to:

6+ months of a previous internship, co-op, or academic project experience outside of normal classes
GPA of 3.5 or above

posting.description:
Eligibility:
Current Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD students pursuing degrees in rigorous, highly technical fields (e.g., Computer Science, Computer Engineering) who are eligible for full-time roles starting in 2028 or 2029.
Program Length:
10 Weeks (Early June – Mid August)
Application Process:
Please apply directly through this posting. Applications are reviewed and candidates will progress on a rolling basis. You can anticipate receiving feedback on your application within 3 weeks.
PDT Partners – a quantitative investment manager - is seeking talented engineering students for Software Engineering focused internships. We are looking for interns who can add to a company that values creativity, energy, and collaborative problem solving.
Throughout our 10-week program, students work closely with supportive senior developers on individual projects, receive hands-on personalized mentorship, and contribute to PDT's culture through both intern and company wide social events.
Why join us?
PDT Partners has a 30+ year track record and a reputation for excellence. Our goal is to be the best quantitative investment manager in the world—measured by the quality of our products, not their size. Our people come from diverse disciplines, are intellectually extraordinary and our community is close-knit, down-to-earth and collaborative.
Internship Projects
Software Engineers at PDT are responsible for building and maintaining the technology the enables all parts of the trading life cycle. As a software engineering intern, you will work closely with expert developers on technically challenging projects to design, develop, debug, and test our software components for large handling of financial data, real-time events, and batch processing.
Depending on the specific project, you may:
Face problems that don't have well-defined solutions - creativity will be essential to come up with the best possible answers, including ones that explore new technologies
Learn about financial markets and quantitative trading
Build an understanding of various trading technologies and make contributions to them
Develop tooling used for infrastructure management
Contribute to the infrastructure and maintenance of large-scale data sets
The internship offers opportunities to correctly apply new idioms, techniques, and algorithms in select areas, which may include:
Program correctness - resource management, exception safety, reentrancy/thread safety
Maintainability - portability, good coding practices, adherence to coding standards, unit testing, documentation
Efficiency - optimal data structures/algorithms, understanding of high-/low- level implications and trade-offs in design choices, parallelization
Below is a list of skills and experiences we think are relevant. Even if you don’t think you’re a perfect match, we still encourage you to apply because we are committed to developing our people.
Excellent academic background from a rigorous computer science or engineering program graduating in Fall 2027 or later
Strong programming skills with a deep understanding of data structures and algorithms
Fast-learner, intellectually curious, problem-solving approach
Proactive with sense of urgency
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Interest in working in a world-class, professional environment
Committed to improvement and keen to apply constructive feedback
The salary for this role is $180,000.
This amount is not inclusive of any potential bonus amounts.
PRIVACY STATEMENT: For information on ways PDT may collect, use, and process your personal information, please see PDT’s privacy notices.
NOTE: PDT does not currently offer a quantitative research internship program. However, we hire for full-time quantitative research roles on a rolling basis.

With over 500,000 customers who have utilized more than $1 billion in spending power, we are at a pivotal moment. We are scaling our operations, building new offerings, and deepening our impact. We are looking for teammates eager to join us on this journey.
Our venture partners include First Round Capital and L Catterton.
Products we’ve built to make an impact:
Perpay Marketplace: Combines interest-free payments and modern e-commerce to reduce cost of ownership and promote healthy repayment behavior.
Perpay+: Leverages Marketplace repayment history to help members monitor and build credit with all 3 credit bureaus.
Perpay Credit Card: Expands access to the flexibility and benefits of a World Mastercard by removing common barriers like high security deposits and low approval odds.
Our team thrives on in-person collaboration, operating from our unique center-city Philadelphia office. This comfortable "home away from home" space offers river views and fosters rapid product development, strong relationships, and career growth. The energy from achieving big wins is palpable here. While we primarily work in the office, we offer sensible flexibility for personal needs, such as sick children or urgent errands, and coordinate official remote weeks around major holidays. If you are passionate about a meaningful mission, collaboration, equity, and generous perks, Perpay is the best place to be in Philadelphia right now.
About the Role:
As an intern at Perpay, your main responsibility is to learn. We understand the value of mentorship and offer students an opportunity to gain real work experience before graduation. In the 10-12 weeks we'll be together next summer (2027), you will have the opportunity to uncover and communicate insights from our company data that will inform decision-making on open and pressing business questions.
Candidates hired for this role will be placed on one of the following teams based on fit and business need, determined after the hiring process:
Strategic Analytics
Risk
Business Planning & Analysis (BP&A)
In close collaboration with team members on your assigned team, you will apply rigorous research approaches to frame analyses impacting key areas of the business, create high-quality analytic code to assemble evidence, and communicate clear and actionable recommendations to leadership based on your research. All while developing the skills to succeed in a fast-paced tech start-up environment and experiencing and contributing to our unique culture.
Our greatest strength is our people, and we'd love for you to be one of them!
What You’ll Bring:
Currently enrolled in or will receive a Bachelor's/Master's in a quantitative discipline with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and June 2028, or equivalent relevant experience
Knowledge of statistical research methods
Experience using SQL for acquiring and transforming data
Experience programming for data analysis and visualization (Python preferred)

Bonus:
Enrolled in a Master’s Degree or advanced technical degree
Previous work experience in a technical field

we know not everybody checks all the boxes, so if you’re interested, please apply because you could be just what we’re looking for!

Relay Launchpad Intern: Software Engineer (AI/ML) – Summer 2027
Relay, a dynamic and rapidly growing tech startup based in Raleigh, is on a mission to revolutionize frontline work. For decades, technology has supercharged the desk worker while leaving behind the 80% of the global workforce who don’t sit at a desk. The builders, the caregivers, the operators, the movers—the frontline—still rely on walkie-talkies, paper notes, and shouted instructions.
At Relay, we believe it’s time for a change. Our smart, rugged radios and connected cloud ecosystem harness the power of voice and AI to close this digital chasm. We’re building tools that meet frontline workers where they are, capturing tribal knowledge, and turning communication into action. By transforming every spoken word into intelligence, we’re delivering safety, productivity, and empowerment to the workers who keep our world moving.
We are looking for a motivated and ambitious undergraduate (or graduate) student expected to graduate in December 2027 or Spring 2028 to join our Engineering team for a
paid Internship during the summer 2027
. High-performing interns may be considered for full-time roles after graduation, depending on business needs.
Take a look at our website at
relaypro.com
Job Overview
This internship offers a chance to build technology that matters—products that directly empower frontline workers. You’ll collaborate with engineers in a high-growth environment, helping to develop tools that turn voice into structured data, integrate AI into workflows, and make communication instantly actionable.
Interns will gain hands-on experience across the engineering stack, from core product functionality to tools that accelerate development to AI-powered experiences that put intelligence directly into the hands (and voices) of frontline teams.
Summer interns are expected to work full-time in-office during the summer in our amenity rich, world class headquarters in Raleigh, NC.
We use a diverse set of languages, including Python, Erlang, Elixir, Rust, and Javascript. Our systems are generally Linux-based. Our culture is based on Impact, Team, and Learning.
What You Will Do
Work in close coordination with other engineers to contribute to product functionality, enablement tools, and issue resolution.
Analyze requirements to determine feasibility, propose architectures, assess risk, and estimate effort.
Participate in the team’s software development process and tooling, gaining real-world Agile experience and getting code into production.
Develop automated tests to ensure quality, reliability, and performance.
Research and share best practices in software development, including AI/ML applications, to continuously raise the bar for the team.
Collaborate with engineers to identify opportunities for machine learning solutions and stay current on the latest AI/ML advancements.
Assist in designing, training, and evaluating machine learning models using techniques such as supervised, unsupervised, and deep learning.
Help prepare and preprocess datasets—including data cleaning, feature engineering, and data augmentation—to improve the efficiency of model training.
Work alongside the engineering team to integrate ML models into production systems, with a focus on scalability and reliability.
What You Will Bring
Undergraduate or graduate student at a university in Raleigh, Durham, or Chapel Hill with an expected graduation date of December 2027 or Spring 2028.
Currently enrolled in Machine Learning, Computer Science, or a related technical field with a
GPA of 3.5 or above.
1+ years of development experience.
Strong machine learning skills, including designing new ML models, implementing training harnesses, and optimizing inference engines, through prior experience, coursework, or personal projects.
Ability to thrive in a collaborative team environment and show empathy for colleagues.
Strong communication and problem-solving skills.
Commitment to tackling challenging problems with curiosity and initiative; eager to learn and grow.
Care deeply about quality and customer experience, building elegant, simple, and valuable solutions.
Adaptable to change and motivated to contribute independently when needed.
Evaluate ideas based on merit and consistently seek to generate customer value.
Some experience with Python and familiarity with a machine learning framework such as PyTorch or JAX (coursework and research experience counts).
Desired, but not required: experience with LLMs, context management, or applied AI/ML projects.

You'll collaborate with engineers in a high-growth environment, working on custom communication devices at the heart of the Relay platform, from application-layer features to deep OS and hardware integration.
Interns will gain hands-on experience across the full device stack, from Android application development and OS-level systems programming to embedded firmware and Linux hardware interfaces — contributing to a product that ships to real customers every 6 weeks.

Relay
is the Intelligent System of Action for the physical economy. While the digital revolution has often left the deskless workforce behind, we are closing that gap by transforming analog frontline operations into a data-rich, AI-powered ecosystem. We aren't just selling radios, we’re building the digital foundation for the 80% of the global workforce that doesn't work at a desk.
Why Join Relay?
A Proven Winner:
Join a hyper-growth company trusted by over 10% of the Fortune 500, continuing to move upmarket with massive impact.
High Value, High Impact:
With 47% of our revenue from $100K+ ARR customers and 135% Net Revenue Retention (NRR), you'll be joining a company rooted in value creation.
Market-Leading Innovation:
The Relay platform captures 1 billion new data points weekly and features award-winning AI tools like TeamTranslate™, with 500% YoY growth.
World-Class Leadership:
Our stellar leadership team is built to help us scale toward our next major milestones.
The Relay Culture:
We’re dedicated to helping you do the best work of your life (BWIML), investing in your growth through L.I.T., living our CHASE values, and learning from incredibly talented, supportive teammates who make the work (and the wins) better every day.
Now, here’s what we’re building, and where you come in.
As a Financial Analyst Intern on the FP&A team, you’ll play a hands-on role during a defining phase of Relay’s growth as we scale towards a potential IPO. Reporting to the Manager, FP&A, you’ll help build and run the planning, forecasting, and reporting engine that informs decisions across the company. We are looking for an exceptional early-career professional — someone with a strong academic record, seeking experience in a rigorous analytical environment, and fluent in modern AI tooling. You’ll work shoulder-to-shoulder with senior business leaders on the real problems that come with scaling a company: thinking critically about how we measure success and the KPIs that matter, driving the annual operating plan for the entire business, and building deliverables for our most senior audiences: the board, investors, and lenders.
What you will do
You’ll work across the full breadth of strategic finance, from partnering with business leaders to the model and reporting that make good decisions possible. As a hands-on member of a small and mighty team, you will:
Partner with business leaders on the decisions that matter.
Work side by side with functional leaders to understand their priorities and the drivers they own, then help quantify, plan, and pressure-test the strategic shifts that move the business forward.
Drive the planning process.
Help run the annual operating plan (AOP) and long-range plan end-to-end; gather inputs from functional owners, use numbers to inform company strategy, and keep the planning process organized and on schedule.
Build, transform, and automate with AI.
Automate data ingestion, reporting, and reconciliation — then go further, finding new ways to bring AI across financial planning and analysis, from sales forecasting to scenario modeling, to transform how the team works and how much it can take on.
Build analyses and recommendations for senior leadership.
Develop analyses, scorecards, and recommendations for the executive team, including the CEO and CFO, by translating the numbers into a clear story with a point of view.
Prepare board, investor, and lender materials.
Help assemble board packages, business reviews, and diligence/data-room materials for investors and lenders.
Define and track the KPIs that matter.
Shape how the business measures success — build and maintain dashboards, deliver clean, trustworthy business intelligence (BI), and keep metric definitions consistent across the team.
Own and extend the financial model.
Help build and improve our driver-based model, refining assumptions, adding scenario layers, sharpening cohort and unit-economics logic, and keeping inputs clean and reconcilable.
Partner on operating expense planning.
Be a key partner to cross-functional teams as they plan and spend for their investments while we scale rapidly, supporting operating expense (OpEx) planning and analysis.
Run recurring reporting and close support.
Produce the monthly operating scorecard and variance packages within days of close and help reconcile actuals quickly and accurately.
What you will bring
Financial foundation:
Previous internship experience in a rigorous, analytically demanding environment (e.g., management consulting, investment banking, private equity, growth equity). You have experience working through ambiguous and challenging problems, you work at pace, and you hold a high bar for quality. Direct FP&A or strategic finance experience and exposure to a B2B SaaS, software, or hardware company are each a plus, but we place most weight on raw analytical horsepower, intrinsic drive to make an impact, and enthusiasm.
Modeling and analytical skills:
Strong Excel/Google Sheets financial modeling skills and a genuine affinity for numbers. You can synthesize information quickly and simplify a complex set of variables into a clear answer.
AI-tooling fluency:
You’re comfortable with — and excited about — using modern AI tools to automate reporting, clean data, and accelerate analysis. You actively look for leverage rather than doing everything manually.
Range over lanes:
You like variety and can flex to wherever the business needs you; OpEx partnering one week, BI/dashboard delivery the next. You’re a versatile generalist.
High-velocity operator:
You have a bias for action and thrive in a fast-paced, ambiguous, build-as-you-go environment. You bring a continuous-improvement mentality to the processes you touch.
Clear communication:
Strong written and verbal skills, with the ability to present financial information clearly to a range of audiences. You’re relationship-oriented and partner well across functions.
Owner mentality:
You take accountability for your work, sweat the details, and follow through by building repeatable processes.
Integrity:
You hold the highest standards of integrity and are trustworthy with sensitive financial information.
Education:
Strong academic record and working towards a Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, Math, or another quantitatively rigorous field, with a track record of high achievement. Familiarity with US GAAP is a plus but not a prerequisite.
Working at Relay
Our Finance team maintains a strong in-office presence to foster creativity and connection. Candidates for this role should expect to work in person 5 days a week at our Raleigh, NC office.
About Relay | Culture, Benefits & Perks
Our culture hinges on Relayers getting
LIT
up in an environment that fosters Learning, Impact, and Teamwork, where we
CHASE
the best work of our lives. We call this
BWIML
(Best Work In My Life).
The future of frontline work is being built here. Come build it with us. We can’t wait to hear from you.

posting.description:
Join us in building the future of finance.
Our mission is to democratize finance for all.
An estimated $124 trillion of assets
will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.
About the team + role
We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.
Our backend engineers sit at the core of how Robinhood works — powering the financial products that millions of people rely on every day. We build and scale the services, infrastructure, and data systems behind brokerage, crypto, payments, and more. We move fast, hold high standards, and solve problems that actually matter — at a scale that very few engineers ever get the chance to touch.
As a Software Engineering Intern, Backend, you won't be on the sidelines — you'll own a meaningful project end-to-end, from initial scoping through to production. You'll be embedded on a real team, working directly with experienced engineers, diving deep into how the US financial system actually operates, and shipping software that meets the correctness and scale requirements of a live financial platform. This is a summer where you'll leave with real impact to show for it!
This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA, Bellevue, WA, or New York, NY office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.
At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.
What you'll do
Own a high-impact backend project from initial scoping through launch — you'll drive the work, not just support it
Partner with a dedicated mentor who will guide you from onboarding through shipping, deepening your understanding of our tech stack and financial domain along the way
Design, build, test, and release software solutions that meet the correctness and scalability requirements of a real financial platform
Collaborate with cross-functional teams across Robinhood to solve critical problems that span the organization
Maintain and scale an existing codebase using technologies such as Python/Django, Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis, Memcached, AWS, and Kubernetes
What you bring
Currently enrolled in a full-time, degree-seeking program with an expected graduation date of Winter 2027 or Spring 2028
Strong CS fundamentals and deep understanding of best coding practices
Solid communication skills and an ability to drive large projects forward in a fast-paced, sometimes ambiguous environment
Passion and interest in financial technology and building fintech products and services
Prior software engineering experience from internships, hackathons, or personal projects
Familiarity with Python/Django or Go, and an understanding of relational databases and transactions
What we offer
Market competitive compensation structure
Quarterly lifestyle wallet for personal wellness, learning and development, and more
Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not
Time away including company holidays, paid time off, and sick time
Lively office environment with catered meals, fully stocked kitchens, and geo-specific commuter benefits
